title: History: formation and consolidation of the EDA and semiconductor-IP industries (1980-2010)
why_it_matters: RU-0011 found EDA founding dates (Mentor 1981, SDA 1983, Synopsys 1986) and the Mead-Conway/DARPA roots, but not the Daisy/Valid era, the ECAD+SDA merger, Mentor/Cadence/Synopsys consolidation, or when IP licensing (Arm, MIPS, Rambus, Artisan, Virage) became a separate business with measurable revenue.
questions: When were Daisy, Mentor and Valid founded and how did workstation-based CAE give way to software-only EDA?
When did Cadence form (ECAD + SDA, 1988) and which acquisitions created today's EDA oligopoly?
When did third-party semiconductor IP become a measurable market and how big was it in 2000 and 2010?
primary_sources: Cadence, Synopsys, Mentor, Arm, MIPS, Rambus, Artisan, Virage 10-K/20-F and S-1 filings (1990s-2000s)
CHM oral histories (Costello, Sangiovanni-Vincentelli, Valid Logic)
EDA Consortium/ESD Alliance historical MSS data

title: History: IDM carve-outs and divestitures of corporate chip divisions (1999-2010) and what happened to their fabs
why_it_matters: Siemens (Infineon 1999), Motorola (Freescale 2004), Agilent (2005), Philips (NXP 2006) and others separated chip units in a short window; RU-0011 recorded the transactions but not the drivers, the later fab closures/sales or the private-equity role.
questions: Why did diversified electronics groups exit semiconductors between 1999 and 2010?
How many fabs did these carve-outs close, sell or convert to fab-lite, and to whom?
What role did private-equity buyouts (NXP, Avago, Freescale) play?
primary_sources: Infineon, Freescale, NXP, Avago 20-F/10-K and IPO prospectuses
Philips, Siemens, Motorola, Agilent annual reports
